mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings expectations, lowering the present value of equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a consecutive monthly series for three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the 20-day IC is statistically indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05) in a 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with stronger consumer demand (GDPC1) and reduces labor market rigidity, accelerating corporate investment and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month growth exceeds 20,000 for two consecutive months and GDPC1 month-over-month growth exceeds 2% in
failure_condition: IC for 60-day forward return is negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) or the correlation between PAYEMS/GDPC1 and 60-day returns is not positive (rho < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 2% in the prior month, investors anticipate future rate cuts and bid up equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly YoY > 2.0% and previous month < 2.0%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are flat or negative, or the 20-day IC is not significantly above zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening demand or supply-side bottlenecks that raise uncertainty, depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or INDPRO shows a sustained upward trend over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains below 1% for three consecutive months in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 anticipates lower borrowing costs and exhibits positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or the 20-day IC is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (PAYEMS) below 4% triggers a wage-price spiral that raises input costs for firms, reducing profit expectations and producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly average < 4% and previous month > 4%
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or wage growth (not directly observable here) is missing a downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback to GDPC1 as proxy) and strong housing starts (not available; fallback to HOUST) together signal robust demand, pushing 20-day S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
failure_condition: 20-day IC is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the proxies move in opposite directions with no alignment to returns.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, reflecting stronger labor market conditions, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative due to higher inflation expectations and tighter financial conditions.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive or the 60-day IC is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE decline.
